epics.ordering_rationale: BW-083 measures the direct-action kernel; isolated family fixtures cannot establish their combined traffic and timing behavior. A small integrated probe retires that risk before cohort expansion while BW-089 and BW-090 retain final recovery and capacity responsibility.

epics.title: Private instance membership and lifecycle
epics.objective: Provide isolated group-owned encounter spaces with controlled admission, departure and reset.
epics.scope: Runtime instance identity, party admission, protected entry/exit, encounter locks and instance cleanup in a single process. Dungeon/raid content and separate-process scheduling remain separate.
acceptance_criteria: Two parties entering the same content receive distinct runtime instances; entities, effects, targeting and chat/interest queries cannot cross the boundary.
Admission checks authoritative membership, capacity, eligibility and encounter state; retries cannot create duplicate occupancy or bypass a lock.
Leaving, disconnecting and rejoining resolve to the configured instance and safe location; an unavailable or closed instance fails safely.
A genuine reset clears encounter-owned hazards, threat, summons and eligibility state without refunding player consumables, resetting cooldown/debt or repeating durable rewards.
Closing an empty or completed instance leaves no orphaned controllable entities or pending ownership claim.
epics.completion_evidence: Required future proof: two-party isolation/admission tests, reconnect and unavailable-instance cases, reset/conservation fixtures and lifecycle diagnostics showing cleanup.
epics.ordering_rationale: Instance isolation is a gameplay/security capability before it is a deployment topology; validate it locally before adding cross-process failure modes.

epics.title: Fenced cross-process character handoff
epics.objective: Transfer a character between two authoritative processes while preserving one owner and committed economic state.
epics.scope: Explicit source suspension, checkpoint, one-use destination proof, epoch claim/revocation and destination snapshot for the currently enabled simple character state. Comprehensive advanced-state certification follows separately.
acceptance_criteria: During handoff new source actions stop; pending economic operations settle or reject before the checkpoint, and committed operations remain durable.
Only the bound destination can consume an unexpired one-use proof for its exact character/checkpoint/epochs; replay, wrong destination and stale epoch reject without spawning another owner.
At every failure boundary one process/epoch retains or recovers authority; the source cannot mutate the character or grant rewards after the destination claim.

Destination state preserves location, current build, long cooldowns and the documented enabled-state checkpoint policy, then reconstructs an owner-private snapshot and independently filtered public view.
Source/destination crash, timeout and disconnect scenarios return the character to a known legal authority/location without duplicating inventory or reversing completed trades.
epics.completion_evidence: Required future proof: two-process fault-injection traces at each handoff boundary, duplicate/expired/wrong-destination proofs, stale-owner reward attempts and inventory/receipt reconciliation across retries.
epics.ordering_rationale: Reserve scope and epoch contracts early, but postpone distributed handoff until local transitions and durable fencing can be observed. One-owner results are required; message delivery is not described as exactly once.

epics.title: Versioned deployment, database migration and rollback
epics.objective: Deploy and replace the small initial service/world deployment without incompatible state or partial economic rollback.
epics.scope: Reproducible release artifacts/configuration, safe admission/drain, database migrations, compatibility checks and rollback/reconciliation. Automatic fleet scaling and independent microservices are not required.
acceptance_criteria: A release identifies the exact client/server artifacts, configuration, content/rules/database versions and supported compatibility; unsupported peers/content reject before mutation.
Planned maintenance stops or redirects admission, settles/rejects outstanding economic work and reports service availability instead of silently dropping committed outcomes.
A migration records planned/validated/applied/failed state and a declared rollback/reconciliation plan; incompatible or failed migration cannot publish an apparently healthy release.
A deployment and rollback exercise preserves operation receipts and both sides of completed transfers/trades across restart; it never independently rewinds combat and currency ownership.
A fresh environment can reproduce the tested release and health diagnostics; failed startup does not accept economic commands.
epics.completion_evidence: Required future proof: staged deploy/update/drain/failed-migration/rollback exercises using the real database, artifact/version manifests, compatibility rejection and post-rollback conservation reports.
epics.ordering_rationale: Use a modest deployable system while interfaces remain separable. Operational reproducibility and rollback are required before expansion; fleet orchestration waits for evidence of need.

epics.title: Content-version migration and readiness admission
epics.objective: Safely replace enabled gameplay content without silently repurposing IDs or leaving illegal builds/items.
epics.scope: Content/rules/database version distinction, affected-record validation, build refund/revalidation and rollout compatibility. Authoring all abilities, recipes and world content belongs to their feature epics.
acceptance_criteria: A content release preserves compatible stable IDs and uses explicit migration for changed meaning; deleted IDs cannot silently identify unrelated content.
Changed talent/ability meaning identifies affected builds and either validates them or applies the documented safe refund/revalidation policy atomically.
Affected item/effect records and equipped budgets are checked before admission; incompatible references or unresolved required bindings keep the package/entry disabled.
Numeric balance changes include affected item/build simulations and clear patch notes linked to exact revisions; structural fixture validity cannot mark runtime evidence passed.
A rejected content update retains the prior valid version; rollout/rollback retains durable economic results and produces an inspectable reconciliation record.
epics.completion_evidence: Required future proof: compatible and breaking content-update fixtures, real migration/refund/revalidation results, invalid-package rejection and staged rollback evidence with affected-record and balance reports.
epics.ordering_rationale: The version boundary is established at project admission. Full migration behavior becomes testable after real builds/items exist, before broad live content changes make recovery expensive.

epics.title: Martial and defensive kit certification
epics.objective: Certify the position, weapon, defense and sequence based specialization cohort.
epics.scope: Warrior/Rogue/Ranger/Monk/Paladin shared kits; their martial specs except Beastmaster/Lifewalker; Skald specialization. Talents are certified in BW-051. Completion requires every documented cohort ability, not a selected enabled subset.
acceptance_criteria: Every documented cohort ability has bound numerical, secondary-effect and resource behavior at its documented unlock level.
Each specialization retains its stated weakness, mandatory role services and two observable contrasting routes.
Stealth, active defense, movement follow-ups and weapon budgets reject invalid states without resets or free generators.
Every enabled ability passes legal, invalid-target and reconnect/reconstruction fixtures, with content IDs recorded.
epics.completion_evidence: Future cohort manifest and executed per-ability fixture report covering Warrior, Rogue, Marksman, Pathfinder, Ironbody, Windfist, Oathkeeper, Crusader and Skald.

epics.title: Offensive caster kit certification
epics.objective: Certify charge, affliction, elemental and paid-contract offensive loops.
epics.scope: Mage/Necromancer/Shaman/Warlock shared kits; Mage specs, Plaguebringer, Soulreaper, Stormcaller, Hellcaller, Pactbinder, Virtuoso and Inquisitor. Completion requires every documented cohort ability, not a selected enabled subset.
acceptance_criteria: Every documented cohort ability binds secondary effects and resource hooks rather than executing free-text intent.
Charges, phase/element sequences, marks and paid clauses follow the single canonical resource policies.
Control-immune enemies retain the explicitly budgeted damage/resource alternative; self-costs remain nonlethal within declared limits.
Legal, invalid-target and reconnect fixtures pass for each enabled ability at its actual unlock.
epics.completion_evidence: Future cohort enablement manifest, resource traces and complete executed ability-fixture report.

epics.title: Healing and prevention kit certification
epics.objective: Certify every healing specialization with sustainable resources and complete role services.
epics.scope: Cleric/Bard shared kits; High Priest, Oracle, Justicar, Minstrel, Grovekeeper, Spiritmender and Lifewalker. Completion requires every documented cohort ability, not a selected enabled subset.
acceptance_criteria: Every healer uses Mana plus only its declared signature state and has affordable direct/group recovery, cleanse and out-of-combat revival.
Effective healing/consumed prevention qualify generators; overhealing and unused shields cannot farm state.
Links, chains, wards, seeds and melee-assisted healing obey recipient caps, eligibility and unique-target policies.
Every documented cohort ability has bound behavior and passes legal, invalid-target and reconstruction fixtures; both factions have common-class healer coverage.
epics.completion_evidence: Future all-healer service matrix, sustained encounter traces and executed ability-fixture results.

epics.title: Summon, form and deployment kit certification
epics.objective: Certify specializations whose identity depends on controlled entities or form state.
epics.scope: Druid shared kit; Gravecaller, Beastmaster, Wildguard, Feral, Starcaller, Totemist and Demonologist. Completion requires every documented cohort ability, not a selected enabled subset.
acceptance_criteria: All documented cohort abilities have bound execution/resource behavior and pass legal, invalid-target and reconstruction fixtures.
One elite versus multiple servants shares one output budget; owner/pet coordination cannot gain from unattended or self-generated loops.
Form and deployment choices retain documented movement, defense and capacity tradeoffs.
Pet paths, recall, replacement, scope loss and encounter resets leave no unauthorized surviving entities.
epics.completion_evidence: Future cohort manifest, path/capacity/transition traces and executed per-ability fixture report.

epics.title: Complete talent binding certification
epics.objective: Certify the documented class and specialization trees against their actual runtime kits.
epics.scope: All 49 trees and 1,764 catalog nodes, including inherited bespoke rules and shared handling contracts; balance evaluation is BW-073.
acceptance_criteria: All 1,764 documented nodes map to explicit supported modifiers/triggers, including the 882 inherited bespoke bindings; no required unresolved behavior remains disabled or is executed as free text.
Each behavior-changing node has an executed positive and exclusion fixture against referenced learned abilities.
All levels admit legal spending within the separate 59/59 budgets, tier gates, exclusive groups and prerequisite graph.
Refunds and loadout application revalidate the whole build and preserve cooldown/debt, state caps and invalid-summon cleanup.
epics.completion_evidence: Future node-to-handler readiness manifest, all-tree capacity results and actual positive/exclusion fixture execution report.
epics.ordering_rationale: Bulk binding follows demonstrated loops and representative build proof; catalog size and schema validity cannot certify meaningful runtime choices.

epics.title: Every-roster beginner certification
epics.objective: Prove the complete opening journey for every documented legal character choice.
epics.scope: All eleven races, both Human allegiances, twelve classes, level-1–10 ability/talent bindings and specialization graduations; full higher-level kit/tree certification remains separate.
acceptance_criteria: Every legal race/faction/class combination creates the reviewed character with only authored legal appearance options.
All 37 specializations graduate alone with functioning starting kits and an intelligible role lesson.
Both factions meet required-path XP, equipment, vendor/recovery and optional profession learning goals.
Fresh-player evaluation covers naming failure, help revisit, death, full bags, shared targets and resume without progression dead ends.
Every early spendable point has legal bound choices; level-54 capstones and later abilities are not required to verify the beginner experience.
epics.completion_evidence: Future coverage matrix, all-specialization graduation fixtures and representative fresh-player usability recordings with findings resolved.
epics.ordering_rationale: Full-roster starter verification needs early-kit bindings, not every high-level ability or capstone. Later cohort certification reuses these fixtures without blocking early player feedback.

epics.title: Personal storage and item mail
epics.objective: Extend item access through the existing ownership and delivery rules.
epics.scope: Personal bank movement and addressed item mail; no separate mail inventory or cross-faction economic bypass.
acceptance_criteria: Bank moves atomically validate owner, stack/version, source and destination; full or stale destinations reject unchanged.
Mail uses the same durable delivery and binding/faction eligibility as other transfers.
Duplicate sends/claims and concurrent equip/trade/withdraw requests preserve a single owned instance.
Opposing-faction alts cannot move prohibited currency/items through storage or mail.
epics.completion_evidence: Future bank withdrawal race, mail replay, full-destination and faction/binding transfer tests.

epics.title: Version-confirmed direct trade
epics.objective: Exchange permitted items and currency only when both players confirm the same offer.
epics.scope: Offer review/confirmation, range/combat/faction checks, atomic settlement and audit receipt.
acceptance_criteria: Any offer edit invalidates both confirmations and the displayed immutable offer version changes.
Commit rechecks ownership, binding, balance, item versions, range, faction and combat eligibility.
Leaving range or disconnecting before commit consumes nothing; postcommit retries return the same result.
Concurrent asset use cannot produce a partial trade, negative balance or duplicated instance.
epics.completion_evidence: Future paired-client trade demonstration and real-store offer-change, disconnect and conflicting-asset tests.

epics.title: Faction-local fixed-price sell listings
epics.objective: Support searchable offline selling through escrowed fixed-price listings.
epics.scope: Listing admission, browse/search, explicit partial fills, fees, expiry/cancel and durable settlement; buyer requests are BW-057.
acceptance_criteria: Only eligible owned items enter escrow before a realm/faction-local listing appears.
Quotes show unit price, quantity, total and versioned fee policy; listing acceptance charges the nonrefundable fee once.
Concurrent last-item purchases, cancellation and expiry yield one valid ownership/currency outcome.
Partial commodity fills require buyer consent and preserve remaining stock; full-bag/retry delivery never repeats settlement.
epics.completion_evidence: Future market race tests, fee arithmetic/receipt evidence and offline-seller delivery demonstration.
epics.ordering_rationale: Listing settlement reuses proven asset invariants. A direct-trade UI is useful prior evidence, but is not a technical prerequisite.

epics.title: Reserved-funds buyer requests
epics.objective: Match eligible sellers against funded purchase requests without creating a second wallet.
epics.scope: Wallet reservations, exact eligible fills, unfilled release and fill/cancel races.
acceptance_criteria: Activation reserves full quantity times unit price in the existing wallet; spendable balance excludes all held funds.
Each accepted fill consumes only its matching reservation, pays the seller less fees and creates delivery once.
Cancellation/expiry releases only unfilled funds without crediting new currency.
Concurrent fills, unrelated wallet debits and repeated cancellation preserve nonnegative balances and a single receipt.
epics.completion_evidence: Future real-database wallet-reservation concurrency and reconciliation results across partial fill/cancel/expiry.

epics.title: Public and addressed crafting commissions
epics.objective: Let customers safely commission exact outputs, including customer-bound challenge components.
epics.scope: Public fixed-tip and private orders, exact quotes, atomic renewable claims, escrow, expiry and settlement; marketplace is independent.
acceptance_criteria: The accepted order fixes blueprint/configuration, result grade, supplied/missing inputs, recipient, fee and expiry.
Two simultaneous claimants produce one bounded renewable lease; uncommitted expiry/cancellation returns customer escrow.
Bound cores remain customer-owned and output is created directly for the customer; crafters gain no copy, appearance or salvage rights.
Commit/cancel/crash/retry races consume inputs, move commission and award skill exactly once, including full-bag delivery.
epics.completion_evidence: Future real-store lease and settlement races, bound-core provenance audit and 100-retry recovery test results.
epics.ordering_rationale: Commissions depend on crafting and asset settlement, not bazaar listings; they can proceed independently once those shared guarantees exist.

epics.title: Versioned recrafting and enhancement services
epics.objective: Change one existing item safely with exact customer-visible consequences.
epics.scope: Grade upgrades, new-band recrafts, sockets/gems/enchant replacement, repairs and instrument configuration through protected service contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Accepted work locks one exact instance/version against equip, trade, market and mail until resolution.
Recraft preserves identity/history while incrementing version; new-band upgrades require declared materials and new equip level.
Preview identifies replaced/destroyed enhancements and binding changes; missing confirmation or incompatibility rejects before consumption.
Reserved enhancement budgets and the two major behavior-effect limit hold after repeated replacement and retries.
epics.completion_evidence: Future recraft/conflicting-use races, enhancement-budget tests and before/after lineage plus customer preview evidence.

epics.title: Cosmetic variants and neutral collections
epics.objective: Deliver authored visual variants without adding combat or economic power.
epics.scope: Inscription presentation glyphs, compatible visual replacements and account cosmetic unlock records.
acceptance_criteria: Only compatible authored variants can be selected; absent assets create no fabricated selectable option.

Variant changes preserve collision, targeting, attack timing, item binding and combat budgets; materials, silhouettes and effects remain compatible with approved pixel scale and never obscure or imitate critical telegraphs.
Account-wide cosmetic access cannot transfer bound assets or bridge opposing faction economies.
Crafted cosmetic output and unlock retries create only the permitted item/collection result.
epics.completion_evidence: Future visual compatibility, no-stat/no-collision and cross-faction collection tests with authored asset references.

epics.title: Portable profession field utilities
epics.objective: Provide limited out-of-combat convenience while preserving public fallback services.
epics.scope: Crafted repair/preparation/station objects, placement, owner limits and preparation categories; no territorial construction.
acceptance_criteria: Each field site permits three utility objects and one active preparation buff per category after five out-of-combat seconds.
Utilities cannot block navigation, create combat collision, occupy objectives or exceed owner limits.
Effects remain equal/weaker substitutes within category caps and both factions have equivalent functionality.
A missing crafter or expired field object never prevents ordinary repair or instance exit.
epics.completion_evidence: Future placement/limit/category tests and multiplayer demonstration against public full-function station fallbacks.
epics.ordering_rationale: Portable repair convenience is assessed against the already working public vendor/repair fallback; combat deployables remain a recommended reuse opportunity rather than a required implementation.

epics.title: Consumable effects and recipient treatment locks
epics.objective: Apply owned consumables through bounded item-use and treatment rules.
epics.scope: Alchemy recovery/defense effects, food preparation, shared cooldown categories and First Aid channels/recipient locks; manufacturing outputs remain with crafting.
acceptance_criteria: Each admitted item-use timing policy commits one owned item and one permitted effect; duplicate requests and concurrent trade/equip use cannot create free or repeated output.
First Aid follows the authored six-second interruptible channel and 60-second recipient treatment lock; damage interruption, concurrent healers and retries cannot bypass the lock or duplicate ticks.
Food/preparation and consumable categories obey their authored caps and fixed level-band effects; old low-band supplies do not scale from a high-level consumer’s maximum resources.
Mode restrictions, invalid targets and unavailable items produce explicit rejection; UI shows timing, shared cooldown and treatment availability before use.
epics.completion_evidence: Executed consumption, interruption, category and concurrent-treatment fixtures with item/receipt and effective-output traces; reviewed timing bindings for item-use policies.
epics.ordering_rationale: Crafting a numerical item record does not prove that consuming it obeys channel, category and recipient restrictions. Validate item use separately before certifying all profession outputs.

epics.title: Conservative salvage and material conversion
epics.objective: Transform or destroy owned materials without circular value or progression creation.
epics.scope: Declared prospecting/refining/conversion and salvage paths, atomic consumption/output and source eligibility; authoring the full conversion inventory belongs to profession certification.
acceptance_criteria: A declared conversion atomically consumes the exact eligible owned inputs and creates only its authorized output once, including retry, restart and full-bag delivery.
Salvage destroys the source and returns at most 25% of eligible original common materials, zero rare/bound progression cores, zero skill XP and zero gold.
Conflicting recraft/equip/trade/salvage requests yield one permitted item state; reservations or binding cannot be laundered through conversion.
Admission rejects a recipe/vendor conversion graph with an unlimited guaranteed material, currency or progression loop, and retains the failing cycle evidence.
epics.completion_evidence: Real-database concurrent conversion/salvage fixtures and graph validation over declared recipes/vendor values, with loss/conservation traces.
epics.ordering_rationale: A meaningful material-loss/concurrency path can be certified on a small fixture set before the complete recipe catalog; final content must rerun the graph gate.

epics.title: Six-band profession and output certification
epics.objective: Certify the complete profession roster and useful output families across progression.
epics.scope: All 16 professions, 240 mastery nodes and six material bands; expand the 257 representative recipes into the approved release inventory.
acceptance_criteria: Every profession has validated bands 1–300, legal mastery routes and accessible basic training/tools on both factions.
Manufacturing bands provide useful entry, repeat-demand, upgrade and service/tool outputs with exact numerical/binding contracts.
Consumables, bags, tools, shields, instruments, gems, enchants and utility items obey their actual slot/category budgets.
Rare/earned cores are excluded from material-saving effects; gathering, prospecting, salvage and conversion graphs cannot amplify materials or skill indefinitely.
Non-crafters can obtain permitted combat benefits through trade or commissions; no profession grants private raid power.

All 240 mastery nodes have explicit bounded runtime behavior and executed inclusion/exclusion evidence for their product family; training and authored acquisition routes populate retained recipe knowledge rather than making every recipe implicitly known.
epics.completion_evidence: Future approved output manifest, all-band/branch validation, conversion-cycle tests and executed crafting/consumption fixtures.

epics.title: Guild membership and delegated permissions
epics.objective: Let guilds manage members and ranks without granting authority they do not possess.
epics.scope: Guild records, invitations, rank policy, typed membership commands and guild communication; bank assets are BW-064.
acceptance_criteria: Pending invitation expiry/accept/decline/revoke use authoritative time and one terminal result.
Commands enforce exact payload/rank IDs and the caller cannot grant permissions it lacks.
Membership/rank edits invalidate stale views and cannot bypass encounter or invitation constraints.
Guild chat obeys membership, rate limits, mute/block/report and moderation history.
epics.completion_evidence: Future invitation/rank escalation tests, concurrent membership changes and moderated guild-chat demonstration.
epics.ordering_rationale: Party invitations offer useful prior lifecycle evidence, but guild membership/rank authorization can be verified independently with authoritative encounter-lock context. Party/raid frames and formation are not guild prerequisites.

epics.title: Audited guild-bank allowances
epics.objective: Apply shared asset guarantees and rolling member limits to guild holdings.
epics.scope: Deposit, item/currency withdrawal, per-rank policies, allowance reservations and immutable audit.
acceptance_criteria: Zero limits forbid the respective withdrawal kind and configured windows are positive.
Allowance check/reservation, ownership transfer and audit commit together; concurrent withdrawals cannot exceed the limit.
Only committed nonreversed outgoing units/currency count; retries, deposits and rank changes cannot refill allowance.
Unauthorized/stale/conflicting withdrawals reject without lost assets or partial allowance consumption.
epics.completion_evidence: Future real-store simultaneous withdrawal/rank-change tests and replayable allowance/audit reconciliation.

epics.title: Stylized environment and effects integration
epics.objective: Carry the selected 3D pixel-art style through complete gameplay environments without losing combat readability.
epics.scope: Terrain and billboard foliage, stylized water, lighting presets, atmospheric depth, weather/ambient particles and quality tiers. These are presentation requirements, not new weather, swimming or day/night gameplay systems.
acceptance_criteria: Approved outdoor/interior and bright/dark scenes use the shared art conventions; foliage coverage, shadow changes and camera motion preserve readable silhouettes and target markers without unstable flicker.

Water scenes retain correct object/edge visibility above and below the surface, shoreline depth and transparent ordering; the chosen reflection/refraction method and lower-cost alternative pass the same relevant-hazard and privacy checks.

Atmospheric light and rain/dust/splash effects integrate with depth and pixel scale, avoid distracting intersections and have measured per-effect costs; simpler tiers retain the approved atmosphere and gameplay visibility.

Roofs, trees, water and layered floors support a tested occlusion treatment; outline, shadow, reflection, refraction and particle passes consume only authorized views and never reveal concealed or cross-floor entities.

Quality changes and cosmetic substitutions preserve critical telegraphs, selection, aim/ground previews and friendly-frame access in crowded scenes; reduced-flash/shake controls and readable dark presets are verified.

Each supported tier has reproducible scene/settings captures and CPU/GPU/memory measurements including dense foliage, water, atmosphere and overlapping combat effects; expensive effects have bounded budgets and tested alternatives.
epics.completion_evidence: Versioned environment scenes, reference comparison and pass-order recordings, visibility/accessibility fixtures, per-effect profiles and a tested quality/platform matrix.
epics.ordering_rationale: Build on proven camera/material and asset foundations; final presentation and release capacity must include these real effects rather than an empty render scene.

epics.title: Level 11–60 progression journey
epics.objective: Provide an authored, traversable route from beginner departure to the documented level cap.
epics.scope: Release-selected leveling maps, quests, NPC kits, loot and ability-unlock opportunities tested with a declared supported roster; all-roster integration is BW-073, with no invented zone count or lore.
acceptance_criteria: An approved content manifest identifies reachable level-band destinations, quest/encounter rewards and material access through level 60.
Fresh characters progress beyond graduation without missing prerequisites, unavailable destinations or unbound required abilities.
Unlocks at 14/20/22/32/35/44/50 and later talent gates have eligible practice and encounter opportunities.
Required-path reward/credit and recovery checks pass throughout progression; optional professions do not become mandatory combat-point sources.
epics.completion_evidence: Future approved leveling-content scope, path/reward validation and persisted end-to-end progression replays to level 60.
epics.ordering_rationale: Wider-world path/content validation can use the representative roster while other classes bind independently. Exact content volume remains an explicit release-scope decision.

epics.title: Flagged world PvP eligibility
epics.objective: Permit explicit player conflict while protecting unflagged and safe-area characters.
epics.scope: Faction/flag eligibility, confirmed assistance, hostile-participation timers and protected areas; no territory or siege mechanics.
acceptance_criteria: Faction hostility alone never authorizes attacking an unflagged character on the normal ruleset.
Assisting a flagged participant requires confirmation or explicit automatic-flag settings and applies the authored timer.
Protected arrival/recovery scopes reject offensive actions, including indirect pet/area actions.
Normal progression remains in unrated world combat and level/eligibility indicators explain rejection.
epics.completion_evidence: Future cross-faction flag/assist/safe-area matrix including indirect and lingering effects.

epics.title: Consensual nonlethal duels
epics.objective: Resolve bounded player duels without reward or reset exploits.
epics.scope: Mutual invitation, server boundary, surrender, grace, time limit and terminal result.
acceptance_criteria: Only mutually accepted eligible participants enter with explicit positive invitation, boundary/grace and time-limit parameters.
Defeat stops at one health and grants no competitive reward, cooldown reset or resource refill.
Surrender/boundary timeout forfeit; disconnect waits the documented grace, ties draw and invalid protection/scope cancels.
Terminal results and repeated final actions cannot restart the duel or apply ordinary lethal rewards.
epics.completion_evidence: Future lifecycle, timing-boundary and simultaneous-end fixtures plus paired-client duel demonstration.

epics.title: Rated combat normalization
epics.objective: Apply the documented equal-budget rules without altering the saved ordinary build.
epics.scope: Effective level 60, 118-point budget, primary/health ceilings, proportional secondary distribution and effect/consumable disclosure.
acceptance_criteria: Entry computes level-60 normalized primary/health and controlled secondary budgets while preserving proportional selected distribution.
Illegal talents/effects reject or use the explicitly reviewed mode policy; the original ordinary build remains unchanged.
Rated exclusions remove external combat consumables and uncertified set/proc effects; UI explains adjustments before play.
Profession ownership, race cooldowns and challenge-item effects cannot add permanent power beyond the normalized budget.

Before completion, approve the actual-level entry and normalized build/ability-selection policy recorded in open-rated-entry. Every admitted level uses a legal level-60 59/59-point budget; entry, exit and reconnect preserve ordinary earned progression/builds and cannot grant unauthorized ordinary points or ability access.
epics.completion_evidence: Future before/after budget tests over low/normal/challenge gear and representative complete builds, with visible rules disclosure. Include the approved entry/build-selection policy and executed admitted-level, exit and reconnect matrix; unresolved policy prevents completion.
epics.ordering_rationale: Budget normalization can be validated with representative legal kits before the full catalog; roster-specific PvP balance remains a later certification.

epics.title: Instanced five-versus-five objective matches
epics.objective: Run the first complete objective-match lifecycle and record each competitive result once.
epics.scope: Two equal five-player teams, one control point, authored capture/scoring/respawn rules, cancellation and immutable result; queue/ranking algorithms are not invented.
acceptance_criteria: Preparing validates teams, safe spawns and all positive authored timers/score limits before activation.
Uncontested presence captures continuously; contest pauses, empty presence clears unfinished capture and only present uncontested ownership scores.
Score limit wins; timeout uses higher score or draw with no implicit overtime; invalid matches cancel without competitive reward.
Respawn, disconnect and repeated terminal events respect protection, control and normalization rules without duplicate results/rewards.

Any authored participation/reward grant checks current mode eligibility and commits once per match/recipient; cancellation grants no competitive reward and duplicate terminal events create no second grant.
epics.completion_evidence: Future automated objective timeline tests, result-idempotency tests and recorded ten-client match under adverse network conditions.

epics.title: Voluntary PvE level-synced builds
epics.objective: Let a player enter lower-level PvE with an explicitly previewed legal effective-level build while retaining their original progression.
epics.scope: Effective-level stat recomputation, eligible ability and point budgets, separately saved downscaled builds or deterministic starter fallback, entry/exit preview and restoration; rated PvP normalization remains separate.
acceptance_criteria: Opt-in preview identifies effective level, eligible abilities, recomputed base attributes and separate legal point budgets; downscaling does not multiply the entire original stat sheet.
The original build remains unchanged; selection uses a separately saved valid downscaled build or a deterministic starter build after preview, never arbitrary mid-encounter node removal.
Entry/exit applies a coherent authoritative loadout and rejects invalid/in-combat transitions without partial state, free healing, resource refill or cooldown/debt deletion.
Reconnect and exit restore the appropriate original/effective build and earned progression once; lower-level execution cannot use an ineligible ability or overspend talent points.
epics.completion_evidence: Effective-level stat/allocation and ability-access fixtures, opt-in/fallback UI demonstration, and entry/exit/reconnect tests preserving original build, progression, cooldowns and obligations.
epics.ordering_rationale: PvE downscaling preserves original progression and changes eligible unlocks, unlike rated level-60 normalization. It can be validated on a bounded fixture without waiting for the whole dungeon catalog.

epics.title: Dungeon encounter and loot certification
epics.objective: Deliver the approved five-player dungeon set with composition-independent mechanics and durable outcomes.
epics.scope: Authored encounters, navigation, telegraphs, wipe/reset, reward tables and admission; individual role mechanics were proved in BW-031.
acceptance_criteria: Every release dungeon uses the declared one-tank/one-healer/three-damage baseline with common-class capability coverage.
Common-only, no-Bard, support-DPS and varied melee/ranged groups can solve required mechanics.
Compact/distributed healing and each tank defense category have viable tested responses; immune bosses retain required resource loops.
Wipes, reconnects and repeated completion events preserve reset policy, eligible loot and full-bag delivery without rerolls.
epics.completion_evidence: Future approved dungeon manifest, group-composition completion matrix and executed encounter/reward/recovery tests.

epics.title: Declared-size raid encounter certification
epics.objective: Deliver the approved raid scope without assuming an unmeasured population or mandatory exclusive class.
epics.scope: Authored raid-size decision, encounter/revival pools, role/capability coverage, shared-drop claims and visual readability.
acceptance_criteria: The release manifest declares raid size and encounter budgets; completion evidence measures that size rather than extrapolating to untested larger groups.
Neither faction requires an exclusive aura/class or profession-only buff to satisfy an unavoidable mechanic.
Shared encounter revival charges, control immunity and encounter resets behave consistently under concurrent participants.
Shared drops persist one shuffled claimant order and never reroll on delivery/reconnect; ordinary equipment remains personal.
epics.completion_evidence: Future raid-size review, composition-matrix runs, participant/loot records and measured group readability/load results.
epics.ordering_rationale: Dungeons and a ten-player raid prototype are recommended lower-cost proving grounds. Neither every dungeon nor an arbitrary final raid size is a technical prerequisite; validate the declared scope.

epics.title: Race, faction and equipment parity evaluation
epics.objective: Verify the documented parity constraints across complete builds and gear sets.
epics.scope: All races/roles, fixed offsets, faction mandatory capabilities, adaptive gear and low/normal/challenge complete-set budgets.
acceptance_criteria: Level-60 equal-equipment/build role-output comparisons test highest/lowest racial offsets and the stated less-than-1% target.
Early-level resource breakpoints, healing and survival are measured separately rather than inferred from one primary-stat example.
Complete sets preserve grade/slot, adaptive primary, dual-wield, enhancement and major-effect budgets.
Both factions demonstrate required tank/healer/cleanse/interrupt/revival coverage and report any role-availability risk.
epics.completion_evidence: Future versioned full-set simulations, runtime comparisons and common-provider capability reports with unresolved deviations preventing certification.

epics.title: Leveling and mature-economy relevance evaluation
epics.objective: Prove useful profession access and sustainable asset flow in fresh and established populations.
epics.scope: Level-band usefulness, material accessibility, vendor/conversion loops, market concentration, affordability and sources/sinks; no promised market prices.
acceptance_criteria: Unfunded learners are tested against the documented less-than-30-minute first-useful-output target in each relevant band.
At levels 10/20/30/40/50 every manufacturing profession meets two of slot improvement, distribution change and useful utility for customers.
Both factions have essential materials/recipes and NPC repair/recovery fallback without enemy trade or rare-pattern monopoly.
Fresh/mature scenarios record currency/material sources/sinks, margins, recipe usage, concentration and affordability; no unlimited vendor/craft/salvage cycle remains.
epics.completion_evidence: Future reproducible economic scenarios, real-user relevance tests, conversion graph results and reviewed metric reports.

epics.title: Combat, build and PvP balance certification
epics.objective: Evaluate the complete playable roster with recorded scenarios and explicit uncertainty.
epics.scope: Solo/role encounter output, all 37 specialization routes, PvP matchups, sustain/control/mobility and faction composition; numerical tuning remains versioned.
acceptance_criteria: All 37 specializations have at least two tested legal builds changing at least two decision dimensions while retaining role viability; equal-budget output, survival, control, mobility and ally contribution traces expose their intended tradeoffs.
Solo time-to-kill and healer sustain are measured against prototype expectations; provisional 5% output outliers receive documented investigation.
PvP analysis includes melee uptime, line of sight, pets, healer interruption, pick/exclusion rates and skill/role-matched outcomes.
Human build evaluations identify unusable/filler branches and exploit incentives; the enabled release package records resolutions rather than declaring schema counts balanced.
epics.completion_evidence: Future reproducible simulation/runtime reports, human playtest evidence, balance change history and approved enabled-content manifest.

epics.title: Complete presentation and accessibility certification
epics.objective: Make every enabled gameplay flow readable and operable with the documented input/accessibility options.
epics.scope: Complete 3D pixel-art character/equipment/form and environment inventory, authored animation/audio/icons, creator/build/profession/social/PvP screens, scalable UI and clutter controls; foundations are BW-097/BW-098/BW-099 and BW-028.
acceptance_criteria: Every enabled flow supports remapping, independent UI scaling, readable labels and non-color state cues; supported platforms have declared controller navigation coverage.
Creation and talent editing can be completed by keyboard, with draft undo/search and consequential tooltip previews.

Healers can target friendly frames without clicking world actors; quick-cast retains held preview/cancel, projected ground intent stays aligned across supported windows and rejected actions show specific reasons.

Thirty-player clutter, legal summon density, small-window reflow, bright/dark/wet scenes, foliage/roof occlusion, reduced flashes/shake and audio/subtitle alternatives are evaluated; critical hostile telegraphs stay visible at every supported quality tier.
Animation and sound follow server outcomes/time and never authorize effects or hide unavailable market/craft assets.

The enabled race/class/equipment/form, NPC, environment and cosmetic asset manifest is complete and matches approved reference scenes at gameplay scale; all supported renderer/platform/tier combinations have resolved visual regressions and accessible separate UI.
epics.completion_evidence: Future complete art manifest and reference comparisons, renderer/platform/quality and accessibility/input matrices, crowded-scene motion recordings, small-window captures and resolved human usability findings on exact builds.

epics.title: Advanced-state transfer and recovery certification
epics.objective: Demonstrate that the fully enabled class and profession state survives reconnects, transfer and conservative crash recovery without duplicated power or erased debt.
epics.scope: Cross-system reconstruction regression for statuses/ticks, long cooldowns, summon capacity, forms, songs, signature resources, damage debt and profession jobs. This certifies integration beyond the first handoff. Voluntary effective-level/original build selection is included in the reconstruction matrix.
acceptance_criteria: A graceful transfer preserves permitted status expiry/next-tick/remaining budget, stable cooldown families, damage debt and current build under the declared cleanup/checkpoint policy.
Destination reconstruction leaves exactly one owner summon budget; source pets, links, auras and unattended effects cannot continue granting output after authority ends.

Form/song/resource reconstruction references the same canonical pools and budgets; reconnect/transfer cannot grant health, refill resources, erase debt or bypass cooldowns. Effective-level build selection and its original saved build survive reconstruction without eligibility or point-budget bypass.
Profession jobs and associated receipts settle or resume only under their documented policy; a transfer rejected by a locked transaction cannot duplicate work or refund a committed craft.
Unclean crashes demonstrate the documented conservative recovery point and encounter reset, preserving durable ownership while explicitly reporting lost transient combat state.
epics.completion_evidence: Required future proof: advanced-state reconstruction fixtures and multiplayer fault-injection runs for each enabled mechanic, including reconnect/transfer during a tick, summon replacement, debt payment and profession settlement.
epics.ordering_rationale: Simple handoff should be proven early. Requiring every future class mechanic first delays risk discovery; treating that initial proof as certification of later state is equally unsafe.

epics.title: Measured full-game operational capacity
epics.objective: Establish and verify a defensible supported workload envelope for the intended release configuration.
epics.scope: Simulation, bandwidth, database/settlement and client presentation measurements under crowded gameplay, plus overload/admission behavior. Capacity is a measured release budget, not a speculative realm population.
acceptance_criteria: The approved test plan states concurrency/density, client hardware/platform/renderer/tier/internal resolution, server tick/bandwidth/tail-latency/backlog/memory budgets, client CPU/GPU frame-time percentiles and video-memory budgets, workload mix and failure/recovery objectives before declaring a pass.

Scripted users move, fight, command the maximum legal summons, create overlapping effects, craft and trade; tests include crowded markets/world encounters, burst arrivals and instance activity. Client workloads include the production water/reflection, foliage, lighting/atmosphere and particle configurations rather than only placeholder scenes.

Runs retain tick percentiles, queues, entity/subscription counts, bytes per client, database latency, pending settlements, memory and recovery measurements for exact release versions. Client results retain CPU/GPU frame percentiles, memory/resource counts and expensive-pass timings per supported quality tier.
Latency/loss/jitter/reordering scenarios and an unavailable/saturated destination preserve authorization, meaningful rejection/recovery and economic conservation.
The supported configuration meets approved budgets or explicitly reduces its admission envelope; identified performance changes have before/after evidence and preserve gameplay-critical hazards.
epics.completion_evidence: Required future proof: reproducible full-workload load/soak and client-clutter runs, raw percentile/bandwidth/database reports, approved capacity budgets and overload/recovery evidence for the release configuration.
epics.ordering_rationale: Early probes guide architecture; final capacity waits for the workloads that dominate the intended game. Add partitioning or optimization only where measurements justify it.

epics.title: Full-game integrated regression and balance signoff
epics.objective: Demonstrate the intended game as connected player journeys and resolve release-blocking interaction and balance findings.
epics.scope: Release-candidate integration across characters, level 1–60, enabled roster, groups/PvP, world travel, economy/professions, social systems and presentation. This is evidence of integration beyond individual epic completion.
acceptance_criteria: The release candidate passes a versioned journey matrix spanning both factions, creation through cap, role access, starter departure, group content, professions/economy, social operations and enabled PvP modes.

All 330 documented abilities, all 1,764 talent nodes and the approved full profession/world inventory have current binding and execution evidence; legal/invalid/reconstruction and positive/exclusion fixtures cover required behavior, and no required roster entry remains silently disabled.

Equal-budget build/role/faction and profession-relevance reports meet documented evaluation standards, record measured deviations and resolve or explicitly withhold release on approved blocking findings.

Cross-system failure cases cover concurrent rewards/trades, full-bag delivery, death/logout/reconnect, transition during economic activity, guild permissions and encounter reset without duplicated assets or cleared debt.

Human usability/accessibility sessions cover keyboard talent editing, friendly-frame healing, expensive craft confirmation, small-window reflow and crowded combat, with blocking findings resolved. The release render/asset manifest and supported quality configurations match the approved 3D pixel-art comparisons, with camera/picking, privacy, water/transparency and atmosphere regressions included.
epics.completion_evidence: Required future proof: release-candidate journey matrix, executed integration/fixture reports, balance/profession studies, accessibility sessions and a reviewed issue disposition tied to exact artifacts.
epics.ordering_rationale: Completed subsystem epics do not prove their interaction. Reserve a distinct integration gate, and do not substitute data counts or an unexplained subjective balance claim for measured evidence.

epics.title: Production incident and support recovery rehearsal
epics.objective: Prove that operators can contain and recover realistic failures using the documented tools and authorized procedures.
epics.scope: Service outage, account compromise, economic corruption, failed update and support investigation rehearsals with visible player communications. Routine feature implementation is outside this gate.
acceptance_criteria: A staged outage/overload run uses measured alerts and documented ownership to identify the failure, restrict admission and communicate a user-visible service reason.
An account-compromise scenario revokes access/epochs, preserves permitted evidence and completes authorized recovery/restriction/appeal handling without an undocumented data edit.
An economic incident is contained with scoped freeze/suspension and repaired through audited reconciliation/reversal, preserving both sides of legitimate committed operations.
A failed release/restore rehearsal meets approved recovery objectives or retains a blocking finding; operators verify artifact integrity and post-recovery ownership before reopening.
Support can reconstruct an action history using permitted records; secrets and unnecessary personal data are absent, and retention/access policy is demonstrably enforced.
epics.completion_evidence: Required future proof: dated staged incident transcripts, alert/audit/reconciliation artifacts, measured detection/recovery results and reviewed runbooks corrected by the rehearsals.
epics.ordering_rationale: Backup creation and healthy deployment do not demonstrate operational recovery. Rehearse against the final workload and permission model before the release decision.

epics.title: Production release evidence gate
epics.objective: Make a reviewable release decision from verified full-game, capacity and recovery evidence.
epics.scope: Final artifact/configuration identification, mandatory evidence review, blocking-issue disposition and controlled release acceptance. This is a release gate, not an additional feature bundle or a claim of achieved production readiness.
acceptance_criteria: The candidate identifies immutable artifacts, content/rules/database versions, supported platforms, configured admission envelope and compatibility policy matching the tested reports.
Required feature/integration, security, conservation, capacity, accessibility and recovery evidence is current for the candidate; missing or failed mandatory evidence prevents approval.
Unresolved decisions have approved concrete configuration or an explicit scope exclusion consistent with the intended game; no required documented feature is silently deferred to obtain a pass.
A controlled final deployment validates admission, first login/creation, core gameplay, durable transaction, reconnect and safe rollback checks before production acceptance is recorded.
The release record identifies the responsible approver and retained evidence/findings; approval never changes incomplete epics to Complete without their own verified evidence.
epics.completion_evidence: Required future proof: signed/reviewed release checklist and evidence index, exact candidate manifest, blocking-issue disposition and controlled deployment/rollback smoke results.
epics.ordering_rationale: Release is conditional on demonstrated capabilities, rather than elapsed time, a speculative player count or completion of documentation. Root review must confirm this gate transitively covers every required epic.

milestones.title: Executable ownership proof
milestones.objective: Prove clean runtime artifacts, a versioned content-production route and one durable conflict/crash-safe mutation. Retire the renderer/camera feasibility risk independently.
milestones.outcome: A clean headless fixture run and real-store concurrency/retry/crash evidence exist, with explicit authority/content boundaries. A reproducible reviewed content import/export and invalid-package rejection establish the production route without certifying future handlers. A packaged 3D pixel-art scene demonstrates the chosen visual path and measured target configuration without certifying production art.

milestones.title: Two-client authoritative action
milestones.objective: Expose transport, simulation, disclosure and latency risks with the smallest useful integrated play.
milestones.outcome: Two clients observe one legal movement/action outcome, rejection and late-join recovery; prediction and a repeatable early workload are measured.

milestones.title: Recoverable persistent character
milestones.objective: Make identity, assets, builds and ordinary combat recovery coherent.
milestones.outcome: Create/select a legal character, execute the enabled encounter rules, grant/equip assets and reconnect/crash without duplicated ownership or cleared obligations.

milestones.title: First complete persistent opening playtest
milestones.objective: Validate the documented level 1–10 flow for a representative supported roster and prepare external testing.
milestones.outcome: Warrior/Bard/Mage characters on either faction complete required solo learning/graduation, optional introductions and safe departure; the separate five-player role/build proof, provider security, support controls and real restore pass. Representative starter art uses the approved 3D render view and reusable asset workflow.

milestones.title: Bounded state and world evolution proof
milestones.objective: Retire major state-family and ownership risks before broad kit expansion.
milestones.outcome: Pets, forms, support/debt/periodic families have executable fixtures; isolated local instances, a fenced simple-state two-process handoff and migration/rollback work. This does not claim all advanced state has transferred together. Representative families also pass a combined multi-client impairment/workload probe before broad kit certification.

milestones.title: Full-roster opening and kit certification
milestones.objective: Prove the intended roster and all early legal player journeys.
milestones.outcome: All 12 classes, 37 specializations, 49 trees and documented ability/talent bindings are covered; every legal race/faction/class can reach and complete solo graduation.

milestones.title: Transactional services and profession breadth
milestones.objective: Make the intended trade, guild-bank and profession branches demonstrable.
milestones.outcome: Listings, buyer requests, commissions, recrafts, personal/guild storage and all profession/item-use/conversion families pass contention/conservation checks, with useful six-band outputs and equivalent faction access.

milestones.title: Complete documented playable scope
milestones.objective: Complete the intended level-cap content and cross-family certification evidence.
milestones.outcome: Level 1–60, voluntary PvE level sync, dungeons/raids, flagged/duel/objective PvP, professions/economy, full-state recovery and accessible presentation have certified content and recorded balance/relevance findings. Complete character/environment art and effects pass the supported render-quality matrix.

milestones.title: Production-ready full game
milestones.objective: Accept only a demonstrated full game with measured capacity and recoverable operations.
milestones.outcome: The compatible release candidate passes full-game integration, approved capacity, security/conservation, restore/rollback and incident evidence; controlled deployment and responsible release acceptance are recorded.

sequencing_decisions.title: Authority and the first network proof
sequencing_decisions.choice: Establish server-owned intent/outcome boundaries, then validate two clients with movement and one direct action before the complete combat roster or persistent journey.
sequencing_decisions.alternatives: A client-owned local prototype gives fast visual feedback but cannot test the required concurrent authority. A complete offline combat kernel first is viable, but defers Godot lifecycle/protocol/latency risks. Headless combat fixtures can still develop in parallel with the transport.
sequencing_decisions.basis: Server authority is documented. The size and placement of the first integrated proof are recommendations intended to discover boundary errors at low content cost.

sequencing_decisions.title: Replication grows with executable semantics
sequencing_decisions.choice: Begin with movement/lifecycle revisions and owner/public projections; add casts, statuses, projectiles and recovery state as their rules become executable. Enforce disclosure from the first snapshot.
sequencing_decisions.alternatives: A universal final replication layer before gameplay exists guesses state semantics. Broadcasting all state and hiding it in the client leaks information. Rich spatial tuning can wait for measurements, while privacy and hazard relevance cannot.
sequencing_decisions.basis: Godot provides building blocks, including visibility filtering and value constraints, rather than an MMO authorization policy. Recipient-specific disclosure and correct current-state reconstruction are documented invariants.

sequencing_decisions.title: Prediction before broad usability judgments
sequencing_decisions.choice: Add prediction/reconciliation after authoritative movement and acknowledgments, before interpreting broader movement/combat playtests.
sequencing_decisions.alternatives: Prediction is unnecessary for numerical headless tests or a tightly scoped authority proof. Deferring it until a large content roster risks tuning hazards around zero-latency assumptions. Unlimited historical rewind is neither needed nor part of the baseline.
sequencing_decisions.basis: The target network impairment scenarios are documented; an acceptable correction budget and supported platform envelope must be measured and approved.

sequencing_decisions.title: Small durability proof early; live assets later
sequencing_decisions.choice: Test durable ownership, version conflicts, receipts and crash boundaries early in parallel with simulation; require them before real inventory, rewards and exchanges.
sequencing_decisions.alternatives: Persisting every tick increases cost without the promised exact combat replay. Waiting until all combat is complete postpones the most consequential conservation/concurrency risks. A purely in-memory economy cannot certify restart safety.
sequencing_decisions.basis: Economic acknowledgments must be durable; conservative combat checkpoints/reset are explicitly sufficient. A small conventional relational deployment is the documented starting recommendation, not a hard requirement for independent microservices.

sequencing_decisions.title: Stable boundary contracts, incremental binding
sequencing_decisions.choice: Preserve IDs, versions, authority, coordinate scope, explicit rejection and compatible wire values first. Bind only enabled records and expand concrete content with executed fixtures. A versioned author/import route produces these packages; migration/admission are distinct consumers of that route.
sequencing_decisions.alternatives: Freezing every future final payload delays gameplay learning on unauthored content. Inventing disconnected local models now creates integration debt. Existing complete contracts constrain behavior without claiming their handlers exist.
sequencing_decisions.basis: All 29 recorded contract questions are resolved; 329 ability and 882 inherited talent bindings remain runtime/content work. Documentation completeness is not implementation readiness.

sequencing_decisions.title: Commitment before effects; representative mechanics before volume
sequencing_decisions.choice: Prove legal targeting, cost/timing commitment and numerical resolution before mass ability expansion. Validate statuses, hazards, signature resources and representative advanced state as distinct capabilities. Combine the representative families in one measured multi-client probe before broad cohort certification.
sequencing_decisions.alternatives: Implementing all classes first repeats mistakes across hundreds of bindings. Requiring every effect family before one network action overextends the first experiment. Mandatory level-ten roles already need signature state, so deferring every advanced resource until after the starter is also unsound.
sequencing_decisions.basis: Reservation/release/interrupt behavior, bounded triggers, role services and reconstruction are explicit requirements; grouping families into small risk probes is the scheduling judgment.

sequencing_decisions.title: Two meanings of playable
sequencing_decisions.choice: Use a minimal technical multiplayer proof first; retain the level 1–10 beginner area as the first complete persistent player journey. Prove a representative supported kit before all-roster graduation certification.
sequencing_decisions.alternatives: Making the full beginner journey the first experiment combines identity, economy, XP, quests and content before authority is checked. Waiting for all 12 classes before any beginner playtest delays useful usability evidence. The representative slice is explicitly incomplete roster evidence.
sequencing_decisions.basis: The beginner requirements mandate solo completion, equivalent faction opportunities, normal unlock levels and enough required XP without optional grinding. They do not mandate that no smaller technical experiment precede them.

sequencing_decisions.title: Local scopes before distributed handoff
sequencing_decisions.choice: Establish zone/floor/instance identity with geometry, build explicit local transitions, then prove a two-process ownership handoff and later full advanced-state reconstruction.
sequencing_decisions.alternatives: Fleet orchestration and seamless travel before an instance works add deployment complexity without a measured target. Deferring epochs/namespaces until production creates duplication/disclosure rework. Small local instances remain a valid independently testable stepping stone.
sequencing_decisions.basis: One owner, one-use transfer proof and safe economic settlement are documented; the separate timing of local and distributed delivery is a recommendation.

sequencing_decisions.title: One asset boundary; parallel service branches
sequencing_decisions.choice: Build inventory/wallet/delivery before exchanges. Direct craft, commissions, direct trade, marketplace and guild bank reuse that boundary but are not forced into a single sequential economy bundle.
sequencing_decisions.alternatives: Requiring the bazaar before commissions is unnecessary: customer escrow can use the same durable ownership without a market listing. Independent custom wallets or guild-bank mutation paths create conservation risks. Profession breadth does not block stable combat.
sequencing_decisions.basis: Bound customer components never belong to the crafter; all transfer channels share eligibility, revisions and receipts. Branch order is flexible once these invariants are executable.

sequencing_decisions.title: Operational capability follows the value at risk
sequencing_decisions.choice: Start with reproducible headless runs, bounded test admission and diagnostics. Add real provider security, privileges and verified restore before persistent external play; prove updates/migrations before ongoing expansion, then certify capacity and incidents on full workloads.
sequencing_decisions.alternatives: A production fleet before evidence delays learning. Leaving security and recovery until release makes persistent playtests unsafe and their results difficult to interpret. Architecture may remain a small deployment until measured capacity requires change.
sequencing_decisions.basis: No concurrency/SLO/recovery objective has already been achieved. Chosen budgets and real restore/rollback exercises are completion evidence, not a checklist of infrastructure products.

sequencing_decisions.title: Renderer feasibility before asset volume
sequencing_decisions.choice: Run a bounded 3D pixel-art camera/material/pass proof alongside headless development, establish reusable art import conventions before starter production, and certify environmental effects and complete assets before final presentation and capacity.
sequencing_decisions.alternatives: Deferring rendering until final polish risks incompatible assets, input projection and platform assumptions. A custom engine fork may be justified by measured gaps, but the reference implementation does not make it mandatory; a stock-build solution or reviewed visual alternative must first be tested.
sequencing_decisions.basis: The user selected David Holland’s 3D pixel-art aesthetic on 2026-10-17. The article documents a custom Godot 4.3 implementation; project settings, current renderer support and acceptable equivalents require revision-specific evidence. This changes presentation, not authoritative movement, targeting or wire encodings.

open_decisions.title: Engine, platform and deployment candidates
open_decisions.description: Select tested Godot/export-template and Unicode-data revisions, supported client platforms, trusted identity provider, persistence implementation and initial hosting. The documented headless/small modular relational approach is a defensible starting recommendation; vendors and capacity are unspecified.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: BW-001/BW-018 choose and demonstrate tested candidates; BW-086/BW-088 verify external-play deployment and compatibility.

open_decisions.title: Capacity, security and recovery budgets
open_decisions.description: Approve concrete per-endpoint lifetimes/limits/retention, expected workload, tick/tail-latency/bandwidth budgets, recovery point/time and release admission envelope. Prototype rates and 20-second grace are starting settings, not established achievements.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Before the relevant security/restore/load epic is Complete; final release cannot accept unnamed or unmeasured targets.

open_decisions.title: Concrete world and starter records
open_decisions.description: Author finite functional maps, appearance assets, starter instructions, NPC kits, loot tables, recovery/exit locations and required XP allocations within existing contracts. No names, lore, branching narrative system or detailed new geography are inferred here.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Representative records before BW-039; full-roster starter and level 11–60 content before BW-052/BW-053, and reviewed release-content manifest before BW-092.

open_decisions.title: Runtime bindings and complete release inventory
open_decisions.description: Prototype profiles do not establish the named secondary ability/talent behavior. The supplied 257 recipes and sample items are representative, not the launch inventory. Decide concrete compatible bindings and complete useful content within the documented class/profession scope.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: BW-047–051 and BW-062 certify the intended full scope; BW-092 rejects missing required roster/content rather than silently shrinking the game.

open_decisions.title: Prices, sources and conversion graph
open_decisions.description: Concrete vendor values, recipe conversion values, source distributions, starter XP allocation and economic tuning need authoring and tests. Published fees, six bands and profession relevance targets remain prototype constraints, not measured health.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Before enabling the relevant vendor/conversion content; economy/profession measurement in BW-072 and final integration in BW-092.

open_decisions.title: Measured balance, usability and content limits
open_decisions.description: Approve balance deviations and launch content bounds using equal-budget role/build/faction tests, actual progression, supported input devices and accessible visual feedback. Twelve classes, 37 specializations and level cap 60 remain requirements; a smaller technical slice is not permission to omit them.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Representative proof before expansion; BW-071–074 and BW-092 resolve release-blocking findings using documented test standards.

open_decisions.title: Incremental topology and comparable branch orders
open_decisions.description: A small deployment with explicit loading transitions can validate the required game before fleet complexity. Full-state conservative recovery is sufficient under the documented baseline; no exact lost-tick replay, unrestricted rewind or seamless travel requirement is added. Social/profession branches can move earlier if team capacity supports them.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Revisit after BW-083/BW-082 measurements and before BW-090 capacity approval; change ordering while retaining IDs if evidence contradicts the assumption.

open_decisions.title: Concrete item-use timing bindings
open_decisions.description: Authored consumable effect records specify effects, channels and category/recipient restrictions. Any unspecified consumption, interruption/refund and treatment-lock start timing needs an explicit reviewed runtime binding before that item is enabled; do not infer it from animation or let duplicate use choose a favorable policy.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Before BW-075 is Complete; preserve published durations, caps, mode exclusions and authoritative conservation.

open_decisions.title: Rated entry eligibility and normalized build selection
open_decisions.description: Rated combat requires effective level 60 and a 118-point budget, but the reference does not specify minimum actual entry level or how a below-cap entrant selects legal normalized talents, role services and ability unlocks. Decide whether entry requires actual level 60 or supports lower-level entrants with an explicitly reviewed temporary build/ability policy. Preserve the required normalization and ordinary earned progression; this audit selects neither alternative.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: Approve before BW-067 can be Complete and before BW-068 admits rated participants. Test admitted-level entry/exit/reconnect, temporary mode selections and unchanged ordinary build/progression; do not infer match initialization or respawn policy from ordinary build application.

open_decisions.title: Render configuration and supported quality envelope
open_decisions.description: The 3D pixel-art direction is selected. Pin the tested renderer/backend/platform envelope, orthographic pitch/framing, internal resolution, pixel scale and aspect/minimum-window policy, asset/material/animation conventions, shadow/outline/pass strategy, environmental quality tiers and client frame/memory budgets. Do not invent fixed resolutions, require an engine fork or promise unsupported renderer parity from the article.
open_decisions.resolution_gate: BW-097 resolves feasibility, camera/display defaults and any engine patch decision; BW-098 fixes production conventions; BW-099 demonstrates environment methods and alternatives; BW-074/BW-090 approve the supported release visual and performance matrix.

deferred_scope: Neutral/cross-faction exchanges, war logistics, timed auctions and financial instruments are outside the baseline economy; neither faction depends on enemy supply. Faction-local fixed-price listings and buyer requests remain required.
Race/faction transfers and class changes are not launch capabilities. Optional cosmetic account collections grant no account-wide combat power or profession throughput.

Housing, territory, sieges, authored geography/lore and long offline manufacturing are outside the current documented baseline. This roadmap requires functional maps/assets/content, without inventing worldbuilding.

Voice chat and seamless travel are optional, not prerequisites. Explicit transitions and a small deployment satisfy the initial topology; larger raid sizes and fleet growth require authored limits and measurements.
No required catalog family is silently deferred beyond the full-game gate. Incomplete bespoke content remains disabled during earlier slices and must be bound/certified for the intended full roster.
critical_review: Moved the durable ownership/recovery probe into the first review group so database correctness can be tested alongside simulation instead of waiting for a full role encounter. It has no combat dependency.

Kept privacy in the initial entity projection and added richer relevance bounds before the first integrated action. Prediction follows authoritative movement but is a recommendation for the technical proof, not a fabricated prerequisite of numerical combat.

Introduced a representative signature-resource probe before role and starter integration; full pets, forms, maintained support and damage-debt families precede roster expansion, rather than every first playable interaction.

Separated a representative beginner playtest from full-roster level 1–10 certification. Optional crafting and grouping remain optional to a player, while the documented introductions still need integration evidence.

Separated local travel and instance identity from cross-process ownership. Simple handoff is tested before final advanced-state recovery; the first handoff does not certify mechanics introduced afterward.

Removed global phase barriers and kept social, profession and economic branches independently actionable. Recommended predecessors express integration convenience; only observable prerequisites are hard edges.

Required provider security and a real restore before persistent external testing, while early headless fixtures and restricted technical sessions stay small. Final capacity and incidents wait for representative full workloads.

Retained separate full-game integration and release gates. Completion percentages describe epic counts only; undefined capacity, balance targets or launch-content bounds cannot be replaced by optimistic status updates.

A competent team could move some profession/social work earlier or defer a simple handoff until larger zones exist. This order favors earlier conservation/ownership learning; it makes no claim that those comparable branch orders have a unique optimum.

Independent audit: retain the initial network/replication order, add explicit content production and a combined-family probe, enforce only demonstrated hard prerequisites, and leave rated entry/build selection as an explicit unresolved policy. See the Roadmap Audit for baseline evidence and per-epic dispositions.

Art-direction revision: replaced the former 2D sprite mandate with the user-selected 3D pixel-art reference.
